# HEM v0.8.1b4 — PID cycles, calibration and stuck-heater detection

A change to a fixed target or a physical device disconnect/reconnect resets the logical PID cycle. The controller retains native minimum run and rest times. Small fluctuations in calculated targets retain their existing tolerance.

Adaptive calibration now requires activity feedback before it credits a running device. An acknowledged thermostat setpoint, a bare ON or a fan speed setting alone cannot train a model. An automatic pause discards the interrupted observation. Completed results and applied gains stay with their operating context.

A supervised heating-only valve can now be monitored when it already reports Off at startup. HEM uses an independent room temperature trend and ignores its own climate entities when checking for competing heaters. A room selection containing both radiator and room probes uses only the independent room readings. Previously configured device and PID-room thermometers are supported. Monitor-only can warn. Monitor and recover can retry the native OFF command at most twice per continuous OFF episode, subject to device permissions. Persistent heating after those attempts needs physical inspection.

Heater-specific recovery now considers the selected weather providers and neighboring room thermometers throughout the observation and again before dispatch. Solar gain, warmer outdoor air, a warmer neighboring room or missing comparison data leave the rise unattributed. A fresh measured valve opening while the heater reports Off provides separate evidence even when there is also external warmth.
